kings1.14.p1.b1.text: At that time Abijah son of Jeroboam became ill…

kings1.14.p1.b2.text: “Now get up, disguise yourself so they will not recognize you as my wife, and go to Shiloh. For Ahijah the prophet is there…”

kings1.14.p1.b3.text: “Take with you ten loaves of bread, some cakes, and a jar of honey, and go to him. He will tell you what will become of the boy.”

kings1.14.p2.b1.text: Jeroboam’s wife did as instructed; she arose and went to Shiloh and arrived at Ahijah’s house. Now Ahijah could not see, for his eyes were dim because of his age.

kings1.14.p2.b2.text: “Behold, the wife of Jeroboam is coming to ask you about her son… when she arrives, she will be disguised.”

kings1.14.p2.b3.text: “Come in, wife of Jeroboam! Why are you disguised?”

kings1.14.p3.b1.text: “…this is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: ‘I raised you up from among the people and appointed you ruler over My people Israel…’”

kings1.14.p3.b2.text: “You have done more evil than all who came before you. You have proceeded to make for yourself other gods and molten images to provoke Me, and you have flung Me behind your back.”

kings1.14.p3.b3.text: “…I will burn up the house of Jeroboam as one burns up dung until it is gone!”

kings1.14.p3.b4.text: “Anyone belonging to Jeroboam who dies in the city will be eaten by dogs, and anyone who dies in the field will be eaten by the birds of the air.”

kings1.14.p4.b1.text: “As for you, get up and go home. When your feet enter the city, the child will die.”

kings1.14.p4.b2.text: “…this is the only one belonging to Jeroboam who will receive a proper burial…”

kings1.14.p4.b3.text: “For the LORD will strike Israel as a reed is shaken in the water…”

kings1.14.p4.b4.text: “So He will give Israel over on account of the sins Jeroboam has committed…”

kings1.14.p5.b1.text: Then Jeroboam’s wife got up and departed for Tirzah,

kings1.14.p5.b2.text: and as soon as she stepped over the threshold of the house, the boy died.

kings1.14.p5.b3.text: And they buried him, and all Israel mourned for him, according to the word that the LORD had spoken through His servant Ahijah the prophet.

kings1.14.p5.b4.text: And the length of Jeroboam’s reign was twenty-two years, and he rested with his fathers, and his son Nadab reigned in his place.

kings1.14.p6.b1.text: Meanwhile, Rehoboam son of Solomon reigned in Judah. He was forty-one years old when he became king, and he reigned seventeen years in Jerusalem…

kings1.14.p6.b2.text: They also built for themselves high places, sacred pillars, and Asherah poles on every high hill and under every green tree.

kings1.14.p6.b3.text: In the fifth year of Rehoboam’s reign, Shishak king of Egypt came up and attacked Jerusalem.

kings1.14.p7.b1.text: …He took everything, including all the gold shields that Solomon had made.

kings1.14.p7.b2.text: Then King Rehoboam made bronze shields in their place…

kings1.14.p7.b3.text: And whenever the king entered the house of the LORD, the guards would bear the shields, and later they would return them to the guardroom.
